title: Zesty Yeasty Malaysian Dough Bao
description: A traditional Malaysian dish featuring a long-fermentation yeasty dough, filled with sweet and savory ingredients, perfect for a snack or dessert. This halal-friendly recipe uses caster sugar and is made with indulgent and velvety textures in mind.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water and yeast, stirring gently to dissolve the yeast.
Add the caster sugar, flour, and salt to the bowl, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Place a tablespoon of melted butter and a sprinkle of coconut milk in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the filling and seal the edges by pressing them together.
Place the buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 15 minutes.
